title: Golden Dragon, Silver Star, and the WPA band with blackface act
summary: Trouble at the Golden Dragon, the Silver Star band, then the WPA bands and blackface park shows with Arthur Seelig.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Some place, I don't know, I'm kind of a little. Yeah. And then there was the Golden Dragon on St. Anne Street. Uh, the Slitko on piano, George Slitko, I haven't seen him for a long time. I think he was in California, he played a fine piano. Uh huh. And uh, we'll see Joe Stevens and myself, the three asses we used to call ourselves. Uh huh. And you know how we lost that, John? Uh huh. Well they had some girl around 18 years old, I was around 18 myself. Uh huh. And uh, they had some fine looking gal there, she sat on George's doctor, can him half a while, and moosed him a little, you know what I mean. Uh huh. She came over to me, almost, almost the uh, the bartender came from behind the public of 38. Uh huh. She said, you dare go so and so, I'm going to kill you. I said, why? I said, you messed up my girl. So man, I started to plead, man. Uh huh. A lot of a job that night again. Yeah. So we had a full round, she said, no, from there, let's see, I went to the Silver Star, which was on St. Claude and St. Bernard. The piano man, and he was, and so I was, uh, his name was, uh, Froger Schiffer. And they had, uh, you see the drum player, his name was Whipple, and that's the same thing. You know, the fellow was talking about. I see myself. And they had, they had some singing waiters there that was rockin' and rustle. And they also had the Negro Floor Shield. And that gun inside, Tyra was sitting with us. What did he play? He played sax, and I tried to teach him the clarinet, but his tone was so bad that he sort of gave it up. And then, and then, and then, and then from there we went, let's see, I was at, that, um, things were extra bad. So they had the ERA and the WPA and also, I got the WPA band. And I was in the military band there. And I had a few dance bands, and they were all, all of the best musicians in the city were on that thing at the time. It was just something that she always had in the pit, like, uh, Henry Raymond and, uh, some old professors, Gene Fonquet, the Papayas, the Chalvin DuPont, Charlie Cadela, Pete Bagova, one of them had bad boys, I used to call him Arthur Del Paget. He was a blackface comedian and drunk player. He had an Evolution Trio years ago. He didn't have, uh, too much nerve at the time. He used to do a lot of blackface. So he, Arthur Celia Gale, we sort of got together at the parks. We started at City Park and St. Rock, you know, Park, and the inner lot. And we used to have around, uh, two or three thousand, two or three thousand other people out there. So we did some blackface acts and he sort of broke me in. It was a lot of fun. I was almost frightened at that, but then, uh, uh, we had a little skit and, uh, we had a jumbo bottle full of, uh, this, you know, muscatel wine. Oh, yeah. And we had a little skit about wine and so forth. He sent me a little drink, Bloody. He used to call him Bloody, you know. Who do they call Bloody? Which one? Uh, uh, he bought bar and left. They both. People used to call each other Bloody. Oh, I see. And then we used to have a jam session in between there, you know. I'd say a half hour or just before the concert was over. We always had a jam session. Obviously, we were going to get to the guitar with Hyman on Susan Boone. Mm-hmm. And Bobo Arden on drums. And Henry Raymond on sax, myself on clarinet. And sometimes Charlie could go up with those sort of players. But he wasn't too, I mean, he didn't, uh, you know, care to play. He started out when I was young and I was trying and he didn't, you know. He was a guy like that. He was, he just got his kicks out of it, you know.

Well, he wanted to help you. He's a nice fellow Charlie. Yeah, yeah, he was one of the best guys I've ever known. I never did know Henry Raymond, but he made some nice records with Detroit. Yeah. Yeah. Let me fix us another drink. I'll have a take for about a while.
